doc.title: Rossano Sportiello interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, October 2, 2015 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Classical training versus the freedom of jazz
summary: Sportiello explains that he felt no freedom in classical playing, so he now brings the freedom of jazz to it; his motto is to play jazz like classical and classical like jazz.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: You mean classical and jazz? Well you know the thing is that I was trained as a classical piano player you know. I graduated at the conservatory in Italy. But my problem with classical was that I never felt the freedom that I could feel by playing popular music or, even better, jazz. And so after the graduation in classical music I stopped almost completely for a few years to play classical and I concentrated only in jazz. But then in the back of my mind there was always like a kind of bothering feeling like I thought it was just too bad to let all that go. And so I said what about if I try little by little to play maybe my recitals, just one classical tune per night. You know? And try to approach classical music with a kind of interior freedom that I normally feel when I play jazz. Now the problem of the freedom with jazz is you feel confident because you know how to improvise. You exactly know the harmonicals, the chords of the tune. you possess the song. So that’s why I think you feel so comfortable. With a movement of a Beethoven sonata, you know, where you have to play exactly everything the way it is written and you have to try to get as close as you can to the idea of the composer, that’s a different task. So they say that some of the greatest classical music performers, when they played one of the great pieces of the repertoire, they made it sound like it was improvised. Because they knew the music so well from the inside, that it almost sounded like they were just making it up on the spot. And so little by little I think I was able to acquire a little bit more freedom in classical music because of — in other words, the jazz thing made me understand how to approach the classical. So my motto is actually you should be playing jazz like classical music because that is where you get the finesse. And then classical music, like jazz, because it has to sound spontaneous. That’s my motto. But I know that many people might not agree with that, but it works for me.
